result:
Servex has stopped crash-looping. The same process (pid 32304) has been up since 04:16 and was still up at 04:22, about six minutes. It has about 300 MB of memory, and the dashboard on port 8090 answers 200.

The cause wasn't the Pool heal/restore code. `sustain` starts Servex with `--import Servex/Crumbs.js`, and Node worker threads inherit that flag. The breadcrumb watchdog worker therefore re-ran `Crumbs.install()` and started another worker, which did the same, without limit. The breadcrumb log showed new `start` lines every ~30 ms and 8 GB of memory just before each exit 134. The main-thread heap stayed at 6 MB throughout. The watchdog came in with `dbcde67f0`.

The fix is in `Servex/Crumbs.js`: `install()` now returns unless it is on the main thread. It passes `node --check` and is committed as `5af4f5188`, so no revert was needed.

I logged the finding and the result in `servex-oom/task.jsonl` (committed separately).
